statBlock.name: Young Kruthik
statBlock.publication: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse
statBlock.description: Young kruthiks start to hunt as soon as they outgrow the nest. They burrow through rock and fight in packs.

sections.Traits:
Pack Tactics. The kruthik has advantage on attack rolls against a creature if one of its allies is within 5 ft. of that creature and is not incapacitated.
Tunneler. It can burrow through solid rock at half its burrowing speed and leaves a tunnel 2½ ft. across.
sections.Actions: Stab. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d4 + 3) piercing damage.
sections.Printed source: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, p. 168.

statBlock.name: Yuan-ti Anathema
statBlock.publication: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse
statBlock.description: An anathema is a yuan-ti abomination transformed by a rite that sacrifices hundreds of snakes and bathes the subject in its enemies' blood. Anathemas do not age and seek sacrifices and riches as they claim divinity.

sections.Traits:
Magic Resistance. The anathema has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
Ophidiophobia Aura. Choose creatures other than snakes or yuan-ti that start their turns within 30 ft. Each must pass a DC 17 Wisdom save or become frightened of snakes and yuan-ti. A frightened target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. A successful save or the end of the effect grants immunity to this anathema's aura for 24 hours.
Six Heads. It has advantage on saves against being blinded, charmed, deafened, frightened, stunned, or knocked unconscious.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack (Anathema Form Only). Make two Claw attacks and one Flurry of Bites attack.
Claw (Anathema Form Only). Melee weapon attack, +10 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 13 (2d6 + 6) slashing damage.
Flurry of Bites (Anathema Form Only). Melee weapon attack, +10 to hit, reach 10 ft., one creature. A hit deals 27 (6d6 + 6) piercing damage plus 14 (4d6) poison damage.
Constrict (Snake Form Only). Melee weapon attack, +10 to hit, reach 15 ft., one Large or smaller creature. A hit deals 16 (3d6 + 6) bludgeoning damage plus 7 (2d6) acid damage and grapples the target (escape DC 16). The creature is restrained and takes the same damage at the start of each of its turns until the grapple ends. The anathema can constrict only one creature at a time.
sections.Spellcasting (Anathema Form Only):
Cast one listed spell as an action, using Charisma (spell save DC 17) and omitting material components.
At will. Animal Friendship (snakes only).
3/day each. Darkness, Entangle, Fear, Polymorph, Suggestion.
sections.Bonus actions: Change Shape. Become a Huge constrictor snake or return to true form. The creature's statistics stay the same, and its equipment does not transform.
sections.Printed source: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, p. 272.

statBlock.name: Yuan-ti Broodguard
statBlock.publication: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse
statBlock.description: Yuan-ti transform captives with a magical brew to create broodguards. They obey yuan-ti instinctively and guard eggs or patrol for intruders.

sections.Traits: Reckless. At the start of its turn, the broodguard can give itself advantage on all melee weapon attacks it makes during that turn. Attack rolls against it then have advantage until the start of its next turn.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Bite attack and two Claw attacks.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d8 + 2) piercing damage.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d6 + 2) slashing damage.
sections.Printed source: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, p. 273.

statBlock.name: Yuan-ti Mind Whisperer
statBlock.publication: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse
statBlock.description: Mind whisperers make a pact with Sseth, the Sibilant Death. They use magic to recruit converts, confuse enemies, and play rival factions against each other.

sections.Traits:
Devil's Sight. Magical darkness does not impede this yuan-ti's darkvision.
Magic Resistance. It has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
Sseth's Blessing. When the yuan-ti reduces an enemy to 0 HP, it gains 9 temporary hit points.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Bite attacks and one Scimitar attack, or make two Spectral Fangs attacks.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d4 + 3) piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) poison damage.
Scimitar (Yuan-ti Form Only). Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d6 + 3) slashing damage.
Spectral Fangs. Ranged spell attack, +5 to hit, range 120 ft., one target. A hit deals 16 (3d8 + 3) psychic damage.
sections.Spellcasting (Yuan-ti Form Only):
Cast one listed spell as an action, using Charisma (spell save DC 13) and omitting material components.
At will. Animal Friendship (snakes only), Message, Minor Illusion, Prestidigitation.
3/day. Suggestion.
2/day each. Detect Thoughts, Hypnotic Pattern.
sections.Bonus actions: Change Shape. Become a Medium snake or return to true form. The creature's statistics stay the same. Its equipment does not transform, and it keeps its current form if it dies.
sections.Printed source: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, p. 274.

statBlock.name: Yuan-ti Nightmare Speaker
statBlock.publication: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse
statBlock.description: Nightmare speakers feed their victims' fears to Dendar the Night Serpent. They interpret the visions Dendar sends as prophecies and act to make them come true.

sections.Traits:
Devil's Sight. Magical darkness does not impede this yuan-ti's darkvision.
Magic Resistance. It has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Constrict and one Scimitar attack, or make two Spectral Fangs attacks.
Constrict. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 10 (2d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage. A Large or smaller creature is grappled (escape DC 14) and restrained until the grapple ends. The yuan-ti can constrict only one creature at a time.
Scimitar (Yuan-ti Form Only). Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d6 + 3) slashing damage.
Spectral Fangs. Ranged spell attack, +5 to hit, range 120 ft., one target. A hit deals 16 (3d8 + 3) necrotic damage.
Invoke Nightmare (Recharges after a Short or Long Rest). Choose one visible creature within 60 ft. Create an immobile illusion of its deepest fear that only it can see. On a failed DC 13 Intelligence save, it takes 22 (4d10) psychic damage and is frightened of the illusion, believing it is real. The yuan-ti concentrates as if on a spell for up to 1 minute, and the illusion cannot be damaged. At the end of each of its turns, the target repeats the save, ending the illusion on a success or taking 11 (2d10) psychic damage on a failure.
sections.Spellcasting (Yuan-ti Form Only):
Cast one listed spell as an action, using Charisma (spell save DC 13) and omitting material components.
At will. Animal Friendship (snakes only), Mage Hand, Message, Prestidigitation.
3/day. Suggestion.
2/day each. Darkness, Fear.
sections.Bonus actions: Change Shape. Become a Medium snake or return to true form. The creature's statistics stay the same. Its equipment does not transform, and it keeps its current form if it dies.
sections.Printed source: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, p. 275.

statBlock.name: Yuan-ti Pit Master
statBlock.publication: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse
statBlock.description: These yuan-ti have snakes in place of arms. They serve Merrshaulk and sacrifice humanoids in the hope of waking him. They favor slow plans that keep yuan-ti cities hidden.

sections.Traits:
Devil's Sight. Magical darkness does not impede this yuan-ti's darkvision.
Magic Resistance. It has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three Bite attacks or two Spectral Fangs attacks.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d4 + 3) piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) poison damage.
Spectral Fangs. Ranged spell attack, +6 to hit, range 120 ft., one target. A hit deals 16 (3d8 + 3) poison damage.
Merrshaulk's Slumber (1/Day). Choose up to five visible creatures within 60 ft. Each must pass a DC 13 Constitution save or fall unconscious in magical sleep for 10 minutes. Damage or another creature spending an action to shake or slap it awakens the target. Creatures immune to being charmed are unaffected.
sections.Spellcasting (Yuan-ti Form Only):
Cast one listed spell as an action, using Charisma (spell save DC 14) and omitting material components.
At will. Animal Friendship (snakes only), Guidance, Mage Hand, Message.
3/day. Suggestion.
2/day each. Hold Person, Invisibility.
sections.Bonus actions: Change Shape. Become a Medium snake or return to true form. The creature's statistics stay the same. Its equipment does not transform, and it keeps its current form if it dies.
sections.Printed source: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, p. 276.

statBlock.name: Zaratan
statBlock.publication: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse
statBlock.description: Summoning this elemental from the Plane of Earth raises the ground into an armored reptile. Its steps can level buildings, and it can draw into its shell to recover.

sections.Damage resistances: Cold, fire, lightning. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Traits:
Legendary Resistance (3/Day). When it fails a saving throw, the zaratan can choose to succeed instead.
Siege Monster. It deals double damage to objects and structures. Earth-Shaking Movement already includes this increase.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Bite and one Stomp attack.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +17 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. A hit deals 28 (4d8 + 10) force damage.
Stomp. Melee weapon attack, +17 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. A hit deals 26 (3d10 + 10) thunder damage.
Spit Rock. Ranged weapon attack, +17 to hit, range 120/240 ft., one target. A hit deals 31 (6d8 + 10) force damage.
Spew Debris (Recharge 5–6). Each creature in a 90-ft. cube makes a DC 25 Dexterity save, taking 33 (6d10) bludgeoning damage on a failure or half as much on a success. A creature that fails by 5 or more is also knocked prone.
sections.Bonus actions: Earth-Shaking Movement. After moving at least 10 ft. on the ground, the zaratan creates a shock wave across a 120-ft.-radius circle centered on itself. That ground is difficult terrain for 1 minute. Each concentrating creature on the ground there loses concentration unless it passes a DC 25 Constitution save. Structures touching the ground in the area take 100 thunder damage. A creature within half the height of a collapsing structure makes a DC 25 Dexterity save. On a failure, it takes 17 (5d6) bludgeoning damage, falls prone, and is trapped and restrained in the rubble. A successful save halves the damage and avoids the collapse’s prone and restrained effects. A buried creature can use an action to escape with a DC 20 Strength (Athletics) check. An adjacent helper within 5 ft. can spend an action clearing debris to grant advantage on the check. With three helpers spending their actions, the check succeeds automatically.
sections.Legendary actions:
The zaratan has 3 legendary actions. Use one option at a time at the end of another creature's turn, spending the listed action cost. Spent legendary actions return at the start of the creature's turn. A creature cannot use these actions while incapacitated or otherwise unable to act. If surprised, it must finish its first turn before using them.
Stomp (1 Action). Make one Stomp attack.
Move (1 Action). Move up to its speed.
Spit (2 Actions). Make one Spit Rock attack.
Retract (2 Actions). Withdraw into its shell. Until it emerges, the zaratan is restrained and has resistance to all damage. Its next legendary action must be Revitalize or Emerge.
Revitalize (2 Actions). Only while retracted, regain 52 (5d20) HP. The next legendary action must be Emerge.
Emerge (2 Actions). Only while retracted, leave the shell and make one Spit Rock attack.
sections.Printed source: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, p. 278.
sections.Table notes: Spit Rock lists 31 fixed force damage or 6d8 + 10 when rolled. The dice average 37.

statBlock.name: Zariel
statBlock.publication: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse
statBlock.description: Once an angel assigned to watch the Blood War, Zariel fell and accepted Asmodeus's offer to rule Avernus. She bargains for the souls of practiced warriors to replenish her legions.

sections.Damage resistances: Cold, fire, radiant. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks that are not silvered.
sections.Traits:
Devil's Sight. Magical darkness does not impede Zariel's darkvision.
Legendary Resistance (3/Day). When Zariel fails a save, she can choose to succeed instead.
Magic Resistance. She has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
Regeneration. Zariel recovers 20 HP at the start of her turn. Radiant damage prevents this recovery at the start of her next turn. She dies only if she begins her turn at 0 HP and does not regenerate.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three attacks using Flail or Longsword in any combination. Replace one attack with Horrid Touch if available.
Flail. Melee weapon attack, +16 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 17 (2d8 + 8) force damage plus 36 (8d8) fire damage.
Longsword. Melee weapon attack, +16 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 17 (2d8 + 8) radiant damage, or 19 (2d10 + 8) radiant damage with two hands, plus 36 (8d8) fire damage in either case.
Horrid Touch (Recharge 5–6). Touch one creature within 10 ft. On a failed DC 26 Constitution save, it takes 44 (8d10) necrotic damage and is poisoned for 1 minute. While poisoned this way, it is also blinded and deafened. It repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.
Teleport. Zariel and her equipment teleport up to 120 ft. to an unoccupied space she can see.
sections.Spellcasting:
Cast one listed spell as an action, using Charisma (spell save DC 26) and omitting material components.
At will. Alter Self (Zariel may become Medium when changing her appearance), Detect Evil and Good, Fireball, Invisibility (self only), Major Image, Wall of Fire.
3/day each. Blade Barrier, Dispel Evil and Good, Finger of Death.
sections.Legendary actions:
Zariel has 3 legendary actions. Use one option at a time at the end of another creature's turn, spending the listed action cost. Spent legendary actions return at the start of the creature's turn. A creature cannot use these actions while incapacitated or otherwise unable to act. If surprised, it must finish its first turn before using them.
Teleport (1 Action). Use Teleport.
Immolating Gaze (2 Actions). Choose one visible creature within 120 ft. It must pass a DC 26 Wisdom save or take 22 (4d10) fire damage.
sections.Lair actions:
Zariel can choose one of the following options at initiative count 20, losing ties. An option cannot be used in consecutive rounds.
Fireball. Cast Fireball.
Infernal Illusions. Cast Major Image four times in different areas without concentration. All four illusions end at initiative count 20 of the next round. Each creature that can see these illusions must pass a DC 26 Wisdom save or be frightened of the illusion for 1 minute. A frightened creature repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.
sections.Regional effects:
Choose one or more effects around Zariel's basalt citadel in Avernus.
Hellscape. Screams and the smell of burning meat fill the area within 9 miles of the lair.
Pyres. Within 1 mile, jets of flame 10 ft. high rise every 60 ft. A creature or object touching a flame takes 7 (2d6) fire damage at most once per round.
Smoke. From 500 ft. out to 2 miles, persistent smoke heavily obscures the area and cannot be dispersed.
After Zariel dies, the effects fade over 1d10 days.
sections.Printed source: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, p. 280.

statBlock.name: Zuggtmoy
statBlock.publication: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse
statBlock.description: The Demon Queen of Fungi spreads spores that turn living creatures into servants and eventually into hosts for fungal growth. Her principal palace on Shedaklah consists of two dozen giant mushrooms linked by shelf-fungus bridges.

sections.Damage immunities: Poison. Nonmagical bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage.
sections.Traits:
Legendary Resistance (3/Day). When Zuggtmoy fails a save, she can choose to succeed instead.
Magic Resistance. She has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three Pseudopod attacks.
Pseudopod. Melee weapon attack, +13 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 15 (2d8 + 6) force damage plus 9 (2d8) poison damage.
sections.Spellcasting:
Cast one listed spell as an action, using Charisma (spell save DC 22) and omitting material components.
At will. Detect Magic, Locate Animals or Plants.
3/day each. Dispel Magic, Entangle, Plant Growth.
1/day each. Etherealness, Teleport.
sections.Bonus actions:
Infestation Spores (3/Day). Create a 20-ft.-radius spherical cloud centered on Zuggtmoy for 1 minute. Any creature inside when it appears or entering afterward makes a DC 19 Constitution save. Success grants immunity to these spores for 24 hours. Failure causes the spores of Zuggtmoy disease until cured or the creature dies. While infected, the creature cannot be reinfected and repeats the save at the end of every 24 hours. A success ends the infection. After three failed repeat saves, fungal growth kills the host and reanimates it as a spore servant if that creature can become one.
Mind Control Spores (Recharge 5–6). Create a 20-ft.-radius spherical cloud centered on Zuggtmoy for 1 minute. Humanoids and Beasts inside when it appears or entering afterward make a DC 19 Wisdom save. Success grants immunity to those spores for 24 hours. Failure causes the influence of Zuggtmoy disease for 24 hours. During that time the creature is charmed by Zuggtmoy and cannot be reinfected by these spores.
sections.Reactions: Protective Thrall. When an attack roll hits Zuggtmoy, redirect that hit to one creature within 10 ft. of her that is charmed by her.
sections.Legendary actions:
Zuggtmoy has 3 legendary actions. Use one option at a time at the end of another creature's turn, spending the listed action cost. Spent legendary actions return at the start of the creature's turn. A creature cannot use these actions while incapacitated or otherwise unable to act. If surprised, it must finish its first turn before using them.
Attack (1 Action). Make one Pseudopod attack.
Exert Will (1 Action). Choose one visible creature charmed by Zuggtmoy. It uses its reaction if available, either to move up to its speed as directed or make one weapon attack against a target she designates.
sections.Lair actions:
Zuggtmoy can choose one of the following options at initiative count 20, losing ties. An option cannot be used in consecutive rounds.
Rally Plants. Up to four friendly Plant creatures Zuggtmoy can see can spend their reactions to move up to their speed and make one weapon attack.
Summon Fungi. Four gas spores or violet fungi appear in unoccupied spaces Zuggtmoy chooses in her lair and vanish after 1 hour.
Unleash Spores. Use Infestation Spores or Mind Control Spores, centering the cloud on a mushroom or other fungus in the lair instead of Zuggtmoy.
sections.Regional effects:
Choose one or more effects around Zuggtmoy's lair.
Corrupted Nature. Within 6 miles, Wisdom (Medicine) and Wisdom (Survival) checks have disadvantage.
Fungal Infestation. Within 6 miles, molds and fungi grow even on surfaces where they would not normally take hold.
Mutating Vegetation. Within 1 mile, parasitic fungi slowly alter the vegetation they infest.
After Zuggtmoy dies, the effects fade over 1d10 days.
sections.Printed source: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, p. 281.
